title: Open-source Toolkit: Benchtop Carbon Fiber Microelectrode Array for Nerve Recording
protocol: Set a soldering iron to 315 °C (600 °F).
Apply flux to all soldering pads on the PCB.
Form small mounds of solder on the back pads of the Flex Array.
Solder the bottom row of connector pins to the back row of solder pads.
Solder the front row of pins to the board by applying a small amount of solder to each pin.
Apply an additional layer of flux if soldering is not happening quickly.
Clean excess flux away with 100% isopropyl alcohol (IPA) and a short bristle brush.
Encapsulate the soldered connections in delayed set epoxy using a 23 G needle and 1 mL syringe placed bevel side down on the pins.
Push epoxy through the syringe slowly so that it flows into and along the connections.
Leave the board overnight so that the delayed set epoxy can cure.
Secure the backside of the board to the sides of the connector by laying a small line of delayed set epoxy across the back side of the board and pulling that onto the edges of the connector.
Leave the board to cure overnight again.
Scoop a small, ~1:1 ratio of silver epoxy in a plastic dish using the wooden ends of two cotton-tipped applicators.
Mix the silver epoxy using the same sticks used to scoop and discard the applicators after mixing.
Cut 2-4 mm off the end of the carbon fiber bundle onto a piece of printer paper using a razor blade.
Pull a laminated piece of paper gently over the top of the bundle to separate the fibers.
Apply silver epoxy between every other pair of traces on one side of the board with the glass capillary.
Take a small drop of epoxy onto the end of a pulled capillary and apply it between every other trace on the end of the board, filling the gap without overflowing.
Use Teflon-coated tweezers to place one carbon fiber in each epoxy trace.
Adjust the carbon fibers so they are perpendicular to the end of the Flex Array board and buried beneath the epoxy.
Place the arrays on a wooden block with fibered ends overhanging the edge of the block.
Bake the wooden block and arrays at 140 °C for 20 min to cure the silver epoxy and lock the fibers into place.
Create a raised adhesive platform within a box so that the bulk of the board can be stuck to the adhesive.
Suspend the fibered ends of the board within the box to prevent fiber breakage.
Store the arrays at room temperature with the fibers suspended in this manner.
Scrape the epoxy out of the traces with a clean pulled glass capillary if fibers pull away from the board.
Apply a small droplet (~0.5 mm in diameter) of UV epoxy on the exposed traces on one side of the board.
Continue to add UV epoxy droplets until the traces are completely covered.
Submerge carbon fibers 1 mm into 1x phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Suspend the silver-silver chloride (Ag|AgCl) reference electrode in the 1x PBS and connect it to the reference of the impedance system being used.
Suspend the stainless steel rod in the 1x PBS and connect to the counter electrode input of the impedance system being used.
Run a 1 kHz impedance scan for each fiber using a potentiostat set to a 1 kHz scan frequency at 0.01 Vrms in a single sine waveform.
Set the potentiostat to 0 V at the beginning of each scan for 5 s to stabilize the recorded signal.
Record the measurements via the potentiostat-associated software.
Rinse the fibers in deionized water by dipping them into a small beaker three times.
Leave the rinsed fibers to dry at room temperature.
Mask the Flex Array connector using the mating connector.
Place a batch of 8-12 arrays into a storage box with a raised adhesive platform so that they can be insulated in one run.
Position the arrays with the connector end on the adhesive platform and the fibered end overhanging.
Coat the arrays in a Parylene C deposition system to a thickness of 800 nm in a cleanroom.
Cut the fibers to 550 µm with surgical scissors.
Use a 532nm Nd:YAG pulsed laser (5 mJ/pulse, 5 ns duration, 900 mW) to cut 50 µm off the tip of the fibers to re-expose the carbon underneath the Parylene C (usually takes 2-3 pulses).
Align the fiber tips using the built-in stereoscope that comes with this laser system.
Cut the fibers to 300 µm with surgical scissors.
Submerge the array in a dish of deionized water, connector side down, and secure it to the bottom of the dish with putty.
Align the fibers with the surface of the water using a pen camera so that the fibers are just touching the surface.
Adjust a butane blowtorch flame to 3-5 mm and run it over the top of the fibers in a back-and-forth motion to sharpen them.
Inspect the array under a stereoscope for pointed tips at 50x magnification.
Cut the carbon fibers to 1 mm with surgical scissors.
Affix a UV laser to three orthogonally configured motorized stages.
Ensure that the laser has continuous beam output for fast and effective alignment and cutting.
Secure the array in place to maintain a still, level plane of electrodes for the laser.
Adjust the distance between the array and the laser so that fibers will be in light with the laser's focal point.
Provide lower power to the laser and adjust distance to best focus on the fiber.
Move the UV laser focal point across the fiber plane at 25 µm/s to cut fibers to a desired length of 500 µm.
Mix solutions of 0.01 M 3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene and 0.1 M sodium p-toluenesulfonate in 50 mL DI water.
Stir the mixture overnight on a stir plate at approximately 450 rpm until no particulates can be observed.
Store the solution in a light-resistant container and refrigerate for up to 30 days.
Run a 1 kHz impedance scan using the same parameters as before in 1x PBS.
Electroplate with PEDOT:pTS to lower the impedance of the electrodes.
Submerge the fiber tips in PEDOT:pTS solution.
Apply 600 pA per good fiber for 600 s using a potentiostat.
Turn the cell off and allow it to rest for 5 s at the end of the run.
Remove the fibers from the solution and rinse them in DI water.
Retake 1 kHz impedances to check that the fibers were successfully coated.
Gently scrape away Parylene C from the ground and reference vias on the board using tweezers.
Short the ground and reference vias together in pairs on this board design.
Cut two 5 cm lengths of insulated silver wire with a razor blade.
Deinsulate the ends of the wires 2-3 mm from one end to be attached to the Flex Array.
Apply a small amount of flux to the vias.
Insert one wire (2-3 mm exposed end) into each ePhys via on the board.
Apply solder to the top of the vias.
Allow the probe to cool, then flip it over.
Apply a small amount of solder to the backside of the via.
Using surgical scissors, snip off any exposed wire sticking out of the back solder mound.
Place the arrays back into the storage box.
Bend the wires back and away from the fiber.
Secure the wires on adhesive tape.
Anesthetize an adult male Long Evans rat using a combination of ketamine (90 mg/kg) and xylazine (10 mg/kg).
Confirm anesthesia with a toe pinch test.
Apply ointment to the eyes to prevent drying during surgery.
Create a 2 mm x 2 mm craniotomy above the right hemisphere's motor cortex.
Identify the lower left corner of the craniotomy by measuring 1 mm anterior of bregma and 1 mm lateral of midline.
Mount the array into a stereotaxic instrument.
Zero the stereotaxic instrument at the dura by gently lowering the fibers until they touch the dura's surface.
Raise the array away from the surgical site and move it to the side until it is ready for insertion.
Resect the dura by gently pulling a needle with a barbed end over the surface of the tissue.
Use a pair of fine forceps to further assist in pulling away the dura once a portion opens to the brain.
Insert the fibers into the craniotomy and 1.2 mm into the brain using a stereotaxic instrument, lowering slowly by hand.
Record ePhys data for 10 min with an ePhys-specific headstage and preamplifier.
Set the preamplifier high-pass filter to process the signal at 2.2 Hz.
Antialias the signal at 7.5 kHz.
Sample the signal at 25 kHz.
Place the rat under isoflurane at 5% under 1 L/min of oxygen until signs of life have ceased (20-30 min).
Confirm euthanasia with decapitation.
Use spike-sorting software to sort and analyze the data using previously reported methods.
Apply a high-pass filter on all channels (250 Hz corner, 4th order Butterworth).
Set the waveform detection level to -3.5 × RMS threshold.
Use a Gaussian model to cluster spikes with similar characteristics.
Combine and average clusters of at least 10 waveforms for further analysis.
Eliminate waveforms that are not spikes from the data set.
Export data after sorting all channels.
Plot and analyze waveforms using analysis software.
Snip off the fibered end of the PCB and mount it on a carbon tape-masked SEM stub.
Place arrays on a platform of stacked carbon tape (4-5 layers).
Sputter-coat the arrays with gold (100-300 Å) following manufacturer procedures.
Image the arrays in an SEM at a working distance of 15 mm and 20 kV beam strength.
